questions.prompt: mini-dsh version 2 opens a folder with only session.v1.jsonl. What happens to that file?
options: It is rewritten in place with the new layout
It is deleted after the new file is written
It keeps every byte, and a new session.v2.jsonl holds the converted events
questions.explanation: The old file is never changed. The converted events go into a new file, so a mistake in a migration can always be checked against the original.

questions.prompt: A file says version 3, and the program knows only up to version 2. What should the program do?
options: Refuse to open it and ask for an upgrade
Treat it as version 2 and continue
Drop the events it does not recognise
questions.explanation: A newer layout may mean things this program cannot know. Guessing could resume a session wrongly, so the program refuses.

questions.prompt: Why does each migration convert only to the next version?
options: Because JSONL files cannot skip versions
Because each change needs one small step, written once, instead of a converter for every pair of versions
Because the model reads one version at a time
Because only the newest version has a header
questions.explanation: Old files reach the current layout by running the steps in order. Each step is written when its change is made, so the work grows by one step per version.
